dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: NROL-172 Clears 57th Mission & 610th Recovery; IFT-12 FAA Approved — Historic Dual-Launch Day (IFT-12 + CRS-34) Set for May 12
heroSubtitle: 8,771 days of SpaceX milestones — On May 11, SpaceX launched NROL-172 (13th Starshield NRO batch) from Vandenberg SLC-4E at 22:28 UTC, marking the 57th orbital mission of 2026 and the 610th cumulative booster recovery (B1103 2nd flight on OCISLY). The FAA simultaneously issued flight safety approval for Starship IFT-12, clearing the final regulatory gate for the Block 3 / V3 Starship maiden flight; NASA held the CRS-34 prelaunch media conference confirming May 12 at 7:16 p.m. EDT launch on track. May 12 now targets two SpaceX launches within ~46 minutes of each other: Starship IFT-12 (Booster 19 + Ship 39 V3, 124.4 m tall, 33 Raptor 3 engines, suborbital arc, first flight of Block 3 architecture) at 5:30 p.m. CDT from Starbase OLP-2, and CRS-34 Cargo Dragon (~6,500 lbs to ISS, Harmony docking May 14) at 7:16 p.m. EDT from SLC-40 Cape Canaveral — what would be the first time any company conducted a next-generation test vehicle launch and an orbital resupply mission on the same calendar day. SpaceX IPO public S-1 filing expected ~May 18–22 (~7 days away); Nasdaq debut targeting June 18–30 at $1.75T valuation.
